title: Probability
shortDescription: Sample space, events, addition and multiplication rules; dice, coins and cards.
genZNote: Probability is just 'how many ways I like ÷ how many ways exist'. The exam only changes the costume: coins, dice, cards, balls.

sections.heading: Core Rules
bullets: P(E) = favourable outcomes ÷ total outcomes; 0 ≤ P ≤ 1; P(not E) = 1 − P(E).
Addition: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B); mutually exclusive: P(A and B) = 0.
Independent events: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B).
With replacement keeps probabilities constant; without replacement changes totals.
Combinations: nCr = n!/(r!(n − r)!) for selection problems.

sections.heading: Standard Spaces
sections.body: Examples: sum 8 with two dice → 5/36. At least one head in two coins → 3/4. King or heart from a pack → (4 + 13 − 1)/52 = 16/52 = 4/13.

table.caption: Reference sample spaces
rows: 6 outcomes; two dice → 36; sum 7 has 6 ways
52 cards; 26 red, 26 black; 13 per suit; 12 face cards; 4 aces

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Probability measures the likelihood of an event as favourable outcomes divided by total outcomes, with rules for combining events.

commonTraps: Do not double count overlaps like king of hearts.
